description: Card P's targets for "Highway tractor 15 L": the invariants are hard; the rest are reported, never failed: their misses are the simulator's to-do list. Predicted strongest lines (not measured: the validation format has no line measure yet): the firing frequency, rpm/60 x 6/2, 32.5 Hz at the 650 rpm idle and 100 Hz at the 2000 rpm limiter.

targets.name: Invariant: starts warm and runs
targets.source: a warm engine started on its key runs and keeps running (engine.state 2)

targets.name: Invariant: within full scale
targets.source: 02-contracts.md, section 1: what process writes is within +-1

targets.name: Invariant: holds its limiter
targets.source: a rev limiter holds the speed within a few percent of where it cuts (some 100 to 200 rpm at 6500)

targets.name: Invariant: pulls away
targets.source: started, in gear and on the pedal, the car moves (a 36 t tractor at least 3 m/s in ten seconds)

targets.name: Invariant: stops at the key
targets.source: the key off stops the engine (engine.state 0 by the run's end)

targets.name: Starts cold
targets.source: a sound engine starts from the air's temperature within some four seconds of cranking and keeps running (a rule of thumb; makers' cold-start specifications are 2 to 5 s)

targets.name: Peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (the maker's ratings, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 14.9 L; 20 to 30 kW a litre

targets.name: Speed at peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (the maker's ratings, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 14.9 L: 1600 to 2000 rpm

targets.name: Peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (the maker's ratings, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 14.9 L; BMEP 16.8 to 23.4 bar (a naturally aspirated petrol engine 10 to 13 bar, turbocharged 18 to 25, a modern truck diesel 20 to 25: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 2)

targets.name: Speed at peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (the maker's ratings, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 14.9 L: 900 to 1300 rpm (a turbocharged engine's plateau: its whole span)

targets.name: Warm idle
targets.source: makers' service specifications of the kind: 600 to 700 rpm warm in neutral (a rule of thumb, firm to 100 rpm); the ECU is asked for 650

targets.name: Idle steadiness
targets.source: a warm idle's speed wanders some 20 to 50 rpm (a rule of thumb); a lope of more than 150 rpm over the range's top is a fault

targets.name: Boost at its target
targets.source: the build's own target (2.60 bar); a wastegate or vane loop holds a steady full load within some 0.1 bar of its target once spooled (makers' boost-control tolerances; judgement)

targets.name: Port gas at full load
targets.source: a diesel's exhaust at the port at full load is some 700 to 1000 K (Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14; makers' pre-turbine limits near 1020 K)

targets.name: Top speed
targets.source: where 0.85 of the kind's published power (375 kW) meets the build's drag area and 1.2 % rolling resistance at 1.225 kg/m^3: 129 km/h, within 7 % (a power balance, not a test)
